cross_fix_conflicts:
Test 3 turned up one real conflict, one incomplete fix and one self-contradiction, all three inside the clusters named in the brief.

1. REAL CONFLICT, inside cluster F-1, between reviewers. design-lens and adversarial both fix surfaceDiffersFromParent by comparing against document.body and KEEP the helper's name. feasibility fixes it by walking up to the nearest painting ancestor and RENAMING the helper to surfaceDiffersFromBackdrop. Either works today (the walk terminates at body, since nothing between paints), but the rename collides with F-3's fix, whose first two anchors were proposed as /surfaceDiffersFromParent\(page, 'player-rail'\)/: apply feasibility's rename and F-3's guard matches nothing, so `pnpm run test:tooling` fails on the very assertion meant to protect the shots. I resolved it two ways at once — F-1 takes the document.body form the orchestrator already spiked (simpler, and not fragile against a future painted wrapper, which adversarial itself flagged as a residual risk), and F-3's anchors are written helper-name-agnostic as `(page, 'player-rail')`, verified to match the assertion, to survive any rename, and to match none of the false positives (the snapshot filename, a bare getByTestId, a prose comment). The two fixes are now independent in either order.

2. INCOMPLETE FIX, inside the F-1/F-2 pair. The brief asked whether a fix to one implies a different fix to the other: it does, and not in the direction adversarial proposed. adversarial's F-2 fix (compare the hovered value against the RAIL's background, mirroring its F-1 fix) does NOT catch hover:bg-elevate reverting to hover:bg-muted — the exact regression the shot's own comment names — because --muted differs from --rail. I spiked all three candidates in Chromium: the 'differs from something' shape cannot work for the ghost hover at all, because that step is a change between two NON-transparent values rather than a surface being present or absent. So the two assertions genuinely need different shapes: F-1 keeps 'differs from the page background', F-2 becomes 'equals --elevate, read through the same serializer'. That is consistent with, not contrary to, the plan's own rule in the Task 5 helper doc-comment that both values must go through one serializer — and it is why I did NOT unify them into one helper.

3. SELF-CONTRADICTION in F-8 as filed. feasibility's fix adds web/README.md to the plan's Modified list, but web/README.md is not in the spec's 'Process changes this carries' list (grepped — the spec names client/README.md only), so the fix silently creates a SECOND out-of-footprint file against the plan's own line 148 ('One file sits outside the spec's stated footprint') and the matching single-file PR-body bullet. Confirmed with the fix extended to update both places.

4. Cluster 3 checked and CLEAN. The Task 3 image-tag guard (F-11) and the Task 9 container-pin assertion do assert about the same literal, but they do not conflict: Task 9 asserts, scoped to the web job, that a pin of the right SHAPE exists (version deliberately loose, /v[\d.]+-noble/), while Task 3 asserts every pin in ci.yml EQUALS the version derived from @playwright/test. F-11's fix touches only the shell-script half, adds no ci.yml assertion, and I verified the strengthened regex passes against the helper exactly as the plan prescribes it. F-3's and F-4's fixes are likewise mutually consistent — both replace a bare substring with an anchored construct, and they pull in the same direction (F-3 is a presence check that prose must not satisfy; F-4 is an absence check that prose must not trip), so neither reintroduces the other's problem. F-12 adds a third assertion to the same file on a different subject, using the same anchoring discipline.

decided_findings.title: Ghost-hover poll compares the hover to its own transparent resting value
decided_findings.section: Task 6: The hover and breakpoint shots — Step 1 (the ghost-hover shot) and Step 4 (its proof)
decided_findings.contradicts: The fix as FILED by adversarial (compare the hovered value against the rail's background) does not contradict another section, but my spike shows it does not catch the regression the plan's own comment names — hover:bg-muted differs from the rail, so it would pass. My after-text replaces it with the token-equality form, which honours the plan's own 'both values through the SAME serializer' rule in the Task 5 helper doc-comment and does not conflict with F-1's document.body fix (different call site, and the two assertions genuinely need different shapes).
decided_findings.spike: Ran a real Chromium probe on Playwright 1.61.1 with the repo's own token values and Tailwind v4's real preflight rule (web/node_modules/tailwindcss/preflight.css:236-252 sets button { background-color: transparent }). Resting is 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)' in all three cases. The plan's `hovered !== resting` PASSES for hover:bg-elevate (correct), hover:bg-muted (the named regression) AND hover:bg-rail (Step 4's own sabotage) — fully vacuous. 'hovered !== rail' catches bg-rail but still passes bg-muted. 'hovered === var(--elevate) read through a throwaway element' is the only form that discriminates: elevate PASS, muted FAIL, rail FAIL, and the token read comes back 'oklch(0.935 0.006 240.4)', character-identical to the hovered computed value.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: The ghost button paints no background at rest (client/src/components/ui/Button/Button.tsx:36-37 gives the variant only hover:bg-elevate and aria-expanded:bg-elevate), and Tailwind's preflight makes every <button> transparent, so `resting` is always 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'. Any opaque hover colour differs from it, so the poll passes under both regressions — including the one Step 4 tells the implementer to plant and expect a failure from.
decided_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `resting` read and assert the hovered background EQUALS --elevate resolved through the same computed-style serializer (a throwaway element carrying background-color: var(--elevate)), and change Step 4's sabotage from hover:bg-rail to hover:bg-muted so the proof plants the regression the shot's own comment names.
decided_findings.why_it_works: Spiked: token-equality is the only form that fails for both hover:bg-muted and hover:bg-rail while passing the correct hover:bg-elevate, and reading the token through a throwaway element returns the identical serialization, so the comparison cannot go green on a format mismatch.
decided_findings.scenario: You are adding the screenshot of a button on the left rail with the mouse resting on it. The plan tells you to prove its colour check works by making the hover colour identical to the rail, so the highlight disappears, then watch the check fail. It passes instead. The button has no colour at all until the mouse arrives, so "the hovered colour is different from the resting colour" is true for every colour you could possibly pick — including both of the broken ones.
decided_findings.triage_note: Applied as recommended: token-equality against --elevate, and Step 4's sabotage moved to hover:bg-muted.

decided_findings.title: Task 8 hook guard is vacuous for three of the four surface assertions
decided_findings.section: Task 8: Guard that the pixel lane actually compares pixels — Step 2 (the hook loop) and Step 4 (proof 4)
decided_findings.contradicts: none — and deliberately so: I made the anchors helper-name-agnostic (`(page, 'player-rail')` rather than `surfaceDiffersFromParent(page, …)`) precisely so this fix survives F-1's rename whether or not F-1 lands. The fix moves in the same direction as F-4's (anchor to the real construct, never a bare substring) and reintroduces none of F-4's problem, because these are presence checks on code, not absence checks over YAML comments.
decided_findings.spike: Assembled the plan's prescribed pages.vr.ts from its own fenced blocks (Tasks 4-7, minus the two prints the plan says to delete) and ran the guard's `sources.some(src => src.includes(hook))` verbatim, then deleted each surface assertion in turn. Only transport-row makes the guard bite — 1 of 4 load-bearing. player-rail survives in the snapshot name 'player-rail-ghost-hover.png'; open-file-button survives in `const ghost = page.getByTestId('open-file-button')`, which the hover needs anyway; engine-error survives in `const panel = page.getByTestId('engine-error')`, in 'player-engine-error.png' and in two prose comments. The `backgroundColor` arm also stays green after deleting any single poll. I then verified four replacement anchors are each unique in the prescribed file and match none of the false positives (snapshot filename, bare locator, prose comment).
decided_findings.whats_wrong: Three of the four names the guard searches for also occur in the same file for reasons unrelated to their surface assertion, so deleting those three assertions leaves the guard green — and Task 8 Step 4's fourth proof, which the plan calls the reason Task 8 exists, prints PASS instead of the quoted failure.
decided_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the four bare-id presence checks with one regex per surface assertion, each anchored to that assertion's own expression — `(page, 'player-rail')`, `(page, 'transport-row')`, `var(--elevate)` and `'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'` — and reword Task 8 Step 4's fourth proof to quote the new message.
decided_findings.why_it_works: Spiked: each of those four strings occurs exactly once in the prescribed shot file, inside the assertion it guards, and none is produced by a snapshot filename, a locator the shot needs anyway, or a prose comment — so deleting any one assertion now turns the guard red.
decided_findings.scenario: You are adding the safety net that fails the build if someone later deletes one of the four colour checks. The plan tells you to test it by removing the left rail's check and watching the build turn red. It stays green. Three of the four names the net looks for also appear elsewhere in the very same file — once in a screenshot's filename, twice in lines the tests need for a different reason — so the net only notices when the fourth one goes.
decided_findings.triage_note: Applied as recommended: one regex per surface assertion, helper-name-agnostic.

decided_findings.title: No permanent guard pins the renamed artifact's upload-to-download pair
decided_findings.section: Task 9, Step 3 — Rename the `vr` artifact and its matching download (and Step 7's guard)
decided_findings.contradicts: none. It adds one assertion to the same test file F-3 and F-4 touch, on a different subject; it neither reuses a bare substring (F-3's problem) nor an unanchored absence check (F-4's problem).
decided_findings.spike: Verified every factual leg in .github/workflows/ci.yml: `playwright-vr-report` appears at line 238 (upload, inside the `vr` job) and line 272 (download, inside `vr-report`); the download step carries `continue-on-error: true` followed by a `[ -f ./vr-artifact/playwright-report/index.html ]` presence gate that makes the job succeed with present=false; and ci-green's needs list is [changes, quality, lint, build, a11y, vr, e2e, secret-scan, sast, deps-cve, pr-title, pr-checklist] — `vr-report` is absent. So a future one-sided rename is silent in all three respects. I also checked the fix is implementable: a `/^\s+name: playwright-\S+$/m` match hits only the artifact names, never a `- name:` step title.
decided_findings.whats_wrong: The rename must land on both halves or the privileged vr-report job silently stops publishing, and nothing in the repo would ever go red: the download is continue-on-error, the presence gate turns a miss into success, and no job waits on vr-report. Task 8 rewrites this guard file's header to claim it pins every CI arrangement whose loss would be silent, and this one is not pinned.
decided_findings.before: (absent — Task 9 Step 3 states the hazard in prose, "Two edits, and they must move together or `vr-report` silently stops finding the report it publishes", and adds no assertion for it)
decided_findings.suggested_fix: In Task 9 Step 7, add one test that slices ci.yml to the `vr` and `vr-report` jobs, reads each block's artifact `name:` under its upload/download step, and asserts the two strings are equal.
decided_findings.why_it_works: It turns the only thing holding the pair together — this PR's manual grep — into a check that survives the PR, so a future one-sided rename fails `pnpm run test:tooling` instead of quietly disarming the hosted diff page.
decided_findings.scenario: Somebody later renames the report file on one side only — in the upload but not the matching download, or the reverse. The job that publishes the picture comparison to a web page quietly finds nothing, reports success, and nothing is waiting on it, so the whole repo stays green. The next person with a failed picture test gets no comparison page at all, and the fastest way out becomes accepting the new pictures without ever looking at them.
decided_findings.triage_note: Chosen over the alternative of narrowing Task 8's header claim; the maintainer picked the test.
